proof_summary: Positivity supplies a decomposition whose associated Sophie Germain prime is \(p=6x-1\) and whose twin pair is \((t,r)=(6y-1,6y+1)\), with \(p+r=6n\). Taking \(n=(N+6)!\), if \(p\le N\) then \(p\mid 6n\) and hence \(p\mid r\), contradicting the primality and size of \(r\); similarly, if \(t\le N\), then \(r\le N+2\), so \(r\mid 6n\) and hence \(r\mid p\), again contradicting primality and size—thus both kinds of primes occur above every bound.
